title: Logic, Bayes and fuzzy reasoning
subtitle: Representing what an agent knows — exactly, probably, or vaguely.

kb.title: Knowledge-based agents and logic
kb.body: A knowledge-based agent stores sentences in a knowledge base and infers new ones. Propositional logic uses true/false statements with ¬ ∧ ∨ → ↔; first-order (predicate) logic adds objects, predicates and quantifiers: ∀x Human(x) → Mortal(x). Inference rules: modus ponens, resolution. Semantic networks, frames and knowledge graphs store facts as nodes and links.
kb.steps: KB: Human(Socrates); ∀x Human(x) → Mortal(x). Instantiate x = Socrates. Modus ponens gives Mortal(Socrates).

bayes.title: Bayes' theorem
bayes.body: P(H | E) = P(E | H) · P(H) / P(E). A disease affects 1% of people; a test detects it 90% of the time (sensitivity) and correctly clears 91% of healthy people (specificity). What is the chance you have it given a positive test? Count 1000 people: 10 are sick, 9 of them test positive; of 990 healthy, 9% = 89.1 also test positive. Of about 98 positives, 9 are truly sick: 9.2%. A low prior keeps the posterior small even for a decent test.

net.title: Bayesian networks
net.body: A Bayesian network is a directed acyclic graph where each node holds P(node | parents). It encodes a joint distribution compactly as a product: P(x₁…xₙ) = ∏ P(xᵢ | parents(xᵢ)). Example: Burglary → Alarm ← Earthquake; Alarm → JohnCalls. Evidence on a leaf updates beliefs about causes.
net.steps: P(B) = 0.001, P(E) = 0.002. Alarm probabilities given (B,E) are listed in its table. The full joint factorises as P(B)P(E)P(A|B,E)P(J|A)P(M|A) — 5 small tables instead of one with 2⁵ entries.

fuzzy.title: Fuzzy logic
fuzzy.body: Real concepts are vague: 28 °C is somewhat warm and a little hot. Fuzzy sets give each value a membership in [0, 1]. A fuzzy inference system has four steps: fuzzify the input (here μcold = 0, μwarm = 0.7, μhot = 0.2), fire the rules (IF warm THEN fan medium…) with strength min(condition), aggregate the clipped outputs, and defuzzify by centroid — here a fan speed of 58.9%.

summary.title: Summary
summary.body:
• Logic: exact. Probability: uncertainty about facts. Fuzzy: vagueness in concepts.
  • Bayes: posterior ∝ likelihood × prior; Bayesian nets factorise the joint.
